mainTopic: Who goes home from the army for a house or vineyard, grafted trees, and a list of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rulings
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a back-and-forth about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule that a man with a stolen house does not go home from the army. Even if the thief repented and paid, he does not go home, because the house first came to him as stolen. Next, a ברייתא explains the פסוק about planting a vineyard. Buying, inheriting, or getting a vineyard as a gift counts, and so do five fruit trees, but not fewer or non-fruit trees. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only real grapevines count, and layering or grafting does not. That clashes with the משנה, and the גמרא offers three answers: רב חסדא's split between forbidden and permitted grafting (with a long search for a real case), רב נחמן בר יצחק's case of a tree layered into a vegetable, and רבי יוחנן's view that the strict ruling is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's own. Along the way רב פפא learns that partners in a vineyard do not go home. The עמוד ends with a list of רבי יוחנן's rulings in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, many about what onlookers might wrongly think, and the list continues on the next דף.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge: by רבי יוסי הגלילי a thief goes home anyway
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a challenge that started earlier: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a thief would leave the army because of his sins, so why does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב need to exclude a stolen house?
steps.simpleTranslation: [He would go home anyway] because of the sins he has.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a challenge that began just before this point. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the army sends home anyone afraid because of his sins, and a thief has a sin in his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught that someone who built a stolen house does not go home. The problem is that by רבי יוסי הגלילי this man goes home anyway, as a sinner. So his teaching seems to clash with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: That are in his hands, meaning sins he is guilty of
The one who is 'afraid and soft-hearted'. By רבי יוסי הגלילי this means afraid because of his sins

phrases.english: because of the sins that are in his hands!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule that a man with a stolen house does not go home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי יוסי הגלילי a thief goes home anyway as a sinner, so excluding him seems pointless

steps.title: Answer: he repented and paid for the house
steps.stepSummary: The rule can fit even רבי יוסי הגלילי: the case is a thief who did תשובה and paid the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. The case is one where he repented and paid the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is a thief who already did תשובה and paid the owner. Since he is no longer a sinner, רבי יוסי הגלילי's 'sins' reason does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the thief repented, he would not be sent home as a sinner. So רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is teaching something new: this man also does not go home for the house itself, since it began as stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. This means the rule can fit even this opinion
Money, the value of the item

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
the case is where he repented
and gave the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the thief repented and paid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A man with a stolen house is a sinner, so he goes home anyway
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a thief who repented and paid. He is no longer a sinner, so the rule teaches something new

steps.title: Challenge: then he is a buyer and should go home
steps.stepSummary: If he paid for the house, he is now like someone who bought it, and a buyer does go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he is a buyer, and he should go home!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Paying for the house should make him a regular buyer, and a buyer does go home from the army.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught that someone who buys a house goes home, just like someone who builds one. So once the thief paid, he seems to fit that rule. That would mean he should go home after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He should go back, meaning go home from the army

phrases.english: If so,
he is a buyer
and he should go back!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָוֵה לֵיהּ לוֹקֵחַ וְלֶיהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a thief who repented and paid still does not go home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying makes him a buyer, and a buyer goes home

steps.title: Answer: it started out as stolen, so he does not go home
steps.stepSummary: Since the house first came to him as stolen property, paying later does not make him a full buyer for this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since from the start it came into his hands as stolen property, he does not go home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the way the house first came to him matters. It began as stolen, so he does not count as a buyer who goes home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying fixes the sin, but it does not change how the house first came into his hands. For this army rule, that first status of גזילה decides the matter. This is the end of the back-and-forth about the stolen house.

keyTerms.meaning: With the status of stolen property

steps.whatToRemember: A thief who repented and paid still does not go home for his house, because it first came to him as גזילה. This is how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule can fit even רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: Since from the start
it came into his hands as stolen property —
no.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא בְּתוֹרַת גְּזֵילָה אֲתָא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: The original status of the house decides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying turns him into a buyer who goes home
steps.terutzMaskana: The house first came to him as stolen, so he does not go home

steps.title: Buying, inheriting, or getting a vineyard as a gift also counts
steps.stepSummary: A new section on the פסוק about planting a vineyard. A ברייתא learns from 'and what man' that a vineyard that was bought, inherited, or received as a gift also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And what man is there that has planted a vineyard...' The רבנן taught: 'That has planted' would only teach one who planted. How do we know about one who bought it, inherited it, or got it as a gift? The פסוק says: 'And what man is there that has planted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה, about a man who planted a vineyard. It brings a ברייתא that widens the rule beyond someone who planted it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we only read 'that has planted', we would think only the planter goes home. The extra words 'and what man is there' are read as including any man who owns a new vineyard, whether he bought it, inherited it, or got it as a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This opens a ברייתא
I only have, meaning this word alone would teach only this
The פסוק says, as the source for the answer

phrases.english: "And what man is there that has planted a vineyard, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
"That has planted" — I only have one who planted.

phrases.aramaic: לָקַח וְיָרַשׁ וְנִיתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה, מִנַּיִן —
phrases.english: If he bought it, inherited it, or it was given to him as a gift, from where do we know?
The verse says: "And what man is there that has planted."
phrases.notes: The extra words 'and what man is there' are what include the buyer, heir, and gift-receiver.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַע כֶּרֶם כּוּ׳״. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the vineyard phrase of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who bought, inherited, or received a vineyard as a gift goes home just like the one who planted it

steps.title: Five fruit trees of any kind also count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'that has planted' also includes five fruit trees, even if they are not grapevines.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Vineyard' would only teach a vineyard. How do we include five fruit trees, even of other kinds? The פסוק says: 'that has planted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now widens the word 'vineyard'. Five fruit trees of any kind also count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כרם alone would mean only grapevines. The words 'that has planted' are read as widening the rule to other planted fruit trees, as long as there are five.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit trees, trees that give food

phrases.english: "Vineyard" — I only have a vineyard;
from where do we include five fruit trees
and even of other kinds?
The verse says: "That has planted."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כֶּרֶם״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֶּרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא continues, now widening the word 'vineyard'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five fruit trees of any kind count like a vineyard for going home from the army

steps.title: Four fruit trees or non-fruit trees do not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sets a limit: four fruit trees are too few, and trees that give no fruit do not count, because the פסוק says 'vineyard'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could I include someone who plants four fruit trees, or five trees that give no fruit? The פסוק says: 'vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops the widening from going too far. The word 'vineyard' sets a limit on what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rule was widened, we might think any planting counts. The word כרם requires something like a real vineyard: enough trees, at least five, and trees that give fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it be? This raises a possible mistake so it can be rejected
Trees that do not give fruit

steps.whatToRemember: A man goes home from the army for a new vineyard he planted, bought, inherited, or got as a gift. Five fruit trees of any kind count, but four fruit trees, or trees with no fruit, do not.

phrases.english: Could it be that I include
one who plants four fruit trees
and five non-fruit trees?
phrases.notes: These are two separate cases: only four fruit trees, or five trees that give no fruit.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Vineyard."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה הַנּוֹטֵעַ אַרְבָּעָה אִילָנֵי מַאֲכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the widening taught in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fewer than five fruit trees, or trees that give no fruit, do not count as a vineyard for this law

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only a real vineyard, and no layering or grafting
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with the ברייתא's first opinion. 'Vineyard' means only grapevines, and the wording 'ולא חללו' leaves out layering and grafting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: 'Vineyard' means exactly what it says. From 'has not used' and 'has not used it,' we learn to exclude one who layers a vine and one who grafts.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא disagrees with the first opinion. It narrows who goes home from war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion counted five fruit trees of any kind. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only grapevines count. He also learns from the extra word 'חללו' ("it") that a man who layered or grafted a vine does not go home.

keyTerms.meaning: as it sounds, in its plain meaning
one who layers, bending a branch into the ground so it takes root
one who grafts a branch onto another tree

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
'Vineyard' means just what it says.
Not just 'has not used' but 'has not used it' —
phrases.notes: דברים 20:6. The extra 'it' tells us the vine must be planted the regular way.

phrases.english: this excludes one who layers and one who grafts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only grapevines count, and layering or grafting does not exempt a man from war.

steps.title: But our משנה counts layering and grafting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the משנה, which lists the one who layers and the one who grafts together with the one who plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: whether one plants, or layers, or grafts, he goes home?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling that layering and grafting do not count. It quotes our own משנה, which says they do count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts planting, layering and grafting all on the same level. That seems to clash directly with the exclusion in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
whether one who plants,
or one who layers, or one who grafts!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The exclusion of layering and grafting in step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly includes layering and grafting, so a ברייתא that excludes them seems to contradict it.

steps.title: Forbidden grafting versus permitted grafting
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction. The ברייתא excludes forbidden grafting, and the משנה includes permitted grafting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: It is not difficult. Here, the ברייתא is talking about forbidden grafting. There, the משנה is talking about permitted grafting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the two sources are talking about two different kinds of grafting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidden grafting means grafting two different kinds of trees together (כלאים). That does not earn a man the right to go home. Grafting that is allowed does count, so the משנה and the ברייתא do not argue.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying grafting never counts. Only forbidden grafting is left out, and permitted grafting still exempts a man.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Chisda:
It is not difficult:
here it is forbidden grafting,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא that excludes grafting.

phrases.english: there it is permitted grafting.
phrases.notes: 'There' is our משנה, which counts grafting.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּהַרְכָּבַת אִיסּוּר, כָּאן בְּהַרְכָּבַת הֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא argue about whether grafting counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidden grafting does not count. Permitted grafting does.

steps.title: What would permitted grafting actually look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real-life case of permitted grafting that would send a man home from war.
steps.simpleTranslation: This permitted grafting: what are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next moves. It asks for a concrete case of the 'permitted grafting' that רב חסדא described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer only works if a real case of it exists. Next the גמרא will try out possible cases one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: what are the circumstances? what case is this?

phrases.english: This permitted grafting —
what are the circumstances?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי הַרְכָּבַת הֶיתֵּר הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the case from step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case of permitted grafting that exempts a man from war

steps.title: Young onto young: he already goes home because of the first tree
steps.stepSummary: If a young tree was grafted onto another young tree, the grafting is pointless. The first young tree already exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a young tree grafted onto a young tree, then let him go home because of the first young tree anyway!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible case and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'young' tree is one he planted recently and has not yet enjoyed. If the base tree is young, he already goes home because he planted it. The grafting adds nothing, so it cannot be the case the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: derive it instead from... (you already have another reason)

phrases.english: If you say a young tree onto a young tree —
derive that he must return
because of the first young tree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא יַלְדָּה בְּיַלְדָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries and rejects the first option for step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining permitted grafting as young onto young
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first young tree already exempts him, so the grafting would make no difference.

steps.title: Rather, young onto old
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is a young branch grafted onto an old tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a young tree grafted onto an old tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a second case where only the grafting could be the reason he goes home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old tree does not exempt anyone. So in this case the only new planting is the young graft, and the grafting really matters.

phrases.english: Rather, a young tree onto an old tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יַלְדָּה בִּזְקֵינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after step 12 failed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Permitted grafting is young onto young.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permitted grafting is young onto old.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a young tree grafted onto an old one is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו taught that a young tree joined to an old tree becomes part of the old tree, with no law of ערלה. So it should not count as a new planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אבהו say: a young tree that was joined to an old tree is cancelled into the old tree, and the law of ערלה does not apply to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'young onto old' case using a rule from רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the young graft loses its status and becomes part of the old tree, it is no longer a new planting. Then it cannot send the man home either.

keyTerms.meaning: is cancelled, loses its own status
the ban on fruit of a tree's first three years

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abbahu say:
a young tree that was joined into an old tree —
the young tree is cancelled into the old tree,
and the law of ערלה does not apply to it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining permitted grafting as young onto old
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The young graft becomes part of the old tree and stops being a new planting, so it should not exempt him.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: young onto young, where the first tree was for a fence or beams
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה goes back to young onto young. The first tree was planted for a fence or for wood, so it does not exempt him, and only the grafted fruit tree does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Really, it is a young tree onto a young tree. The case is where he planted the first tree for a fence or for beams.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה rescues the 'young onto young' case by adding a detail that removes the problem from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the first young tree already exempts him. But if he planted that tree for a fence or for wood, it is not a planting that counts. So the grafted tree, planted for fruit, is the only real reason he goes home.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (going back to an earlier idea)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Really, it is a young tree onto a young tree,
and the case is where he planted that first one
for a fence or for beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם יַלְדָּה בְּיַלְדָּה, וּכְגוֹן דִּנְטַע לְהָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא לִסְיָיג וּלְקוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 14 by going back to the case from step 12 with a new detail
steps.terutzResolutionType: Going back to an earlier case with an added detail (לעולם... וכגון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Young onto young fails, because the first tree already exempts him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Young onto young works if the first tree was planted for a fence or for wood.

steps.title: Support: a tree planted for a fence or beams has no ערלה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that a tree planted for a fence or for wood is exempt from ערלה, so it does not count as a fruit planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who plants for a fence or for beams is exempt from ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רבי ירמיה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a tree planted for a fence or for beams is not treated as a fruit tree for ערלה, it is also not the kind of planting that sends a man home. That leaves the grafted tree as the real reason.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
one who plants for a fence or for beams —
is exempt from ערלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַנּוֹטֵעַ לִסְיָיג וּלְקוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 15
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's claim that a tree planted for a fence or beams does not count

steps.title: Why is a young tree cancelled by an old one but not by a young one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the difference is. Why is a young tree cancelled into an old tree, but not cancelled into a young tree that was planted for wood?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about a young tree onto an old one, that it is cancelled, and what is different about a young tree onto a young one, that it is not cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's case by comparing it to רבי אבהו's rule. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base tree planted for wood is also free of ערלה, just like an old tree. So why shouldn't the young fruit graft be cancelled into it too? Then it would not exempt him either.

phrases.english: And what is different about a young tree onto an old one
that it is cancelled,
and what is different about a young tree onto a young one
that it is not cancelled?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא יַלְדָּה בִּזְקֵינָה דְּבָטְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15 using the rule in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that the young graft is not cancelled into the wood tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both base trees are free of ערלה, so the young graft should be cancelled in both cases.

steps.title: An old tree is locked in, but a wood tree can still become a fruit tree
steps.stepSummary: A young tree grafted onto an old tree cannot go back, so it is cancelled. A tree planted for wood can still be switched to fruit, so it cannot cancel the new tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (the old tree), if he changes his mind about it, it cannot go back. Here (the tree planted for wood), if he changes his mind about it, it can go back, because from the start a tree stands to give fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 17. It explains why a young tree is cancelled into an old tree, but not into a young tree planted for wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a young tree is joined to an old tree, the old tree has taken it over, and this can never be undone. A tree planted for wood only has a weak 'wood' status, because the owner can change his mind and use it for fruit at any time. Something with such an unstable status cannot swallow up a real fruit tree.

keyTerms.meaning: able to go back (to its earlier state)

phrases.english: There, if he changes his mind about it,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the old tree from Step 14.

phrases.english: it is not able to go back;
here, if he changes his mind about it,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the young tree that was planted for a fence or for wood.

phrases.english: it is able to go back,
[since from the start it stands for fruit].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם אִי מִימְּלִיךְ עֲלַהּ — לָאו בַּת מֶיהְדָּר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is the difference' question of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) based on whether the status can be reversed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wood tree is exempt from ערלה just like an old tree, so it should cancel a young tree grafted onto it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The old tree's takeover is permanent. The wood tree's status can change, so it does not cancel the grafted fruit tree.

steps.title: Like trees that grew by themselves
steps.stepSummary: Trees that sprouted on their own are still subject to ערלה, which shows that a tree's natural status is a fruit tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like trees that grew by themselves, as we learned in a משנה: trees that grew by themselves are obligated in ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a משנה. Trees that nobody planted on purpose are still treated as fruit trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody planted these trees with fruit in mind, yet they are still subject to ערלה. This shows that a tree is a fruit tree by default. A 'wood' purpose is only a weak layer on top that can easily fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: It is just like trees that grew by themselves,
as we learned in a משנה:
trees that grew by themselves are obligated in ערלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַעָלוּ מֵאֵילֵיהֶן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the claim in Step 18 that a tree's basic status is a fruit tree.
steps.raayaObject: That a tree naturally stands for fruit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 1:2: trees that grew by themselves are obligated in ערלה.

steps.title: Why not say the vineyard belongs to two partners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it needed the wood-tree case. It could have said the two young trees belong to two partners, so each goes home for his own tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain the case as a vineyard of two partners, where this one goes home for his tree and that one goes home for his tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it chose in Step 15. It suggests a simpler case that seems to work just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two partners each own one of the young trees, each partner has his own new planting. Then there would be no need for the complicated 'planted for wood' idea. Why did the גמרא not just say that?

keyTerms.meaning: let us explain the case as

phrases.english: But let us explain it as a vineyard of two partners,
where this one goes back for his own,
and that one goes back for his own?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ בְּכֶרֶם שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the wood-tree case from Step 15 was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the 'planted for wood' case in Step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler case, two partners, would also give each person a new planting. So why choose a forced explanation?

steps.title: רב פפא: partners in a vineyard do not go home
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the גמרא's choice that a vineyard owned by two partners does not send them home from the war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this teaches that partners in a vineyard do not go back from the war lines for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains why the גמרא did not use the partners case. It does not work, because partners do not go home at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the גמרא went out of its way to avoid the partners case, רב פפא learns a new law from it. A vineyard shared by two owners is not enough to release either of them from the army.
steps.whatToRemember: A vineyard owned by two partners does not send either partner home from war.

phrases.english: רב פפא said: This teaches:
a vineyard of two partners,
they do not go back for it from the war lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by drawing a new law from the גמרא's choice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from what the גמרא avoided
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Partners could each go home for their share.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partners do not go home, so the partners case could not explain the משנה.

steps.title: But five brothers all go home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא from the case of five brothers. When one brother dies in war, all of the others go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from five brothers where one of them died in the war, where all of them go back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's rule. It points to a case where many people sharing one thing all go home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a brother dies without children, any of the remaining brothers may do יבום with the widow. Each of them goes home even though only one will marry her. So why shouldn't each partner go home for a shared vineyard?

phrases.english: And how is it different from five brothers
where one of them died in the war,
that all of them go back?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵחֲמִשָּׁה אַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's rule from Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that partners do not go home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Brothers who share a possible connection to one widow all go home, so partners who share a vineyard should go home too.

steps.title: Each brother can call her 'his wife', but no partner can call it 'his vineyard'
steps.stepSummary: Each brother can marry the widow, so she is fully 'his wife' to each one. A shared vineyard is not fully 'his vineyard' to either partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, each one can be called 'his wife'. Here, no single one can be called 'his vineyard'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking closely at the words of the תורה, 'his wife' and 'his vineyard'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any one of the brothers could end up marrying the whole woman, so for each of them she counts as 'his wife'. A vineyard owned by two people never belongs completely to either of them, so it is not 'his vineyard'.

keyTerms.meaning: we can read (the פסוק's word) about him

phrases.english: There, each and every one,
we can call it 'his wife' about him;
here, each and every one,
we cannot call it 'his vineyard' about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — כׇּל חַד וְחַד קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ ״אִשְׁתּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the brothers challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shared connection should work the same way for brothers and partners.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each brother could have the whole woman. Each partner owns only part of the vineyard, so רב פפא's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Brothers all go home because each can call the widow 'his wife'. Partners do not, because neither can call the vineyard 'his vineyard'.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: grafting a tree onto a vegetable
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different explanation. The grafting in the משנה means grafting a tree onto a vegetable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the case is where one grafts a tree into a vegetable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different case of the 'permitted grafting' from step 10. This replaces the young-tree and old-tree cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first tree-onto-tree cases ran into trouble: young onto young (the first tree already sends him home) and young onto old (the young tree is cancelled). רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a different case of 'permitted grafting': layering a tree into a vegetable, which one תנא allows. Since the tree is not joined onto another tree, those problems do not come up.

keyTerms.meaning: grafts or bends a branch down into the ground

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
It is where one layers a tree into a vegetable,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: בְּמַבְרִיךְ אִילָן בְּיָרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the earlier explanations and gives a new case for the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grafting in the משנה was between two trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grafting in the משנה is a tree grafted onto a vegetable.

steps.title: This follows the תנא who permits grafting a tree onto a vegetable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows a מחלוקת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, in the name of רבי יהודה בן גמדא, permits grafting a tree onto a vegetable, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows this תנא, as taught in a ברייתא: one who grafts a tree into a vegetable, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it in the name of רבי יהודה בן גמדא of the village of Akko, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which תנא holds like רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה can only treat this grafting as a normal planting if it is allowed. רבי יהודה בן גמדא holds it is allowed. So the משנה follows him, while the חכמים, who forbid it, would disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: and it follows this תנא,
as it was taught: one who layers a tree into a vegetable,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits it

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גַּמְדָּא אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ,
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Gamda of the village of Akko,
and the Sages forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא הוּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows which תנא the explanation in Step 24 follows.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה can be about grafting a tree onto a vegetable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the name of רבי יהודה בן גמדא permits it, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation fits only one side of a מחלוקת. The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן גמדא, not the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the ruling follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן says the ruling that a man does not go home for a grafted tree follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי יוחנן said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to solve the contradiction about grafted trees. It says the ruling that a man does not go home for a grafted tree belongs to one specific תנא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא and רב נחמן בר יצחק solved the contradiction by explaining what kind of grafting is meant. רבי יוחנן takes a different path. He says the two sources disagree, and the strict one follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings with him
A תנא whose view was quoted earlier in the ברייתא about 'vineyard'

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the contradiction of step 9, alongside the answers of רב חסדא and רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources about grafting seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling that a man does not go home for a grafted tree follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Reading 'planted' exactly as written
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב read 'vineyard' exactly as written, so he also reads 'planted' exactly as written. Only someone who plants goes home, not someone who grafts or layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say there that 'vineyard' means exactly what it says? Here too, 'planted' means exactly what it says. Someone who plants goes home. Someone who layers or grafts does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ruling fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He reads the words of the פסוק strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said 'vineyard' means only a grape vineyard. With the same strict reading, 'planted' (נָטַע) covers only real planting. Grafting and layering are not planting, so they do not send a man home.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly as the word means, with no widening
Planted, the word used in the פסוק
One who layers a vine, bending a branch into the ground so it takes root

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הָתָם
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov say there
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ברייתא quoted earlier about which vineyard sends a man home.

phrases.english: that 'vineyard' means exactly what it says?
Here too, 'planted' means exactly what it says:
one who plants, yes, goes home;
one who layers or grafts, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הָתָם כֶּרֶם כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for assigning the ruling to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaObject: That the grafted-tree ruling fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the words of this פסוק strictly. 'Vineyard' means only a grape vineyard, and 'planted' means only real planting, not grafting or layering.

steps.title: A very short vine is always treated as ערלה
steps.stepSummary: A young vine shorter than a טפח stays forbidden as ערלה for its whole life, because it looks like a one-year-old vine.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: A young vine shorter than a טפח is forbidden as ערלה all its years, because it looks like a one-year-old vine.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב has been mentioned, the גמרא begins a list of other rulings that רבי יוחנן said in his name. The first ruling is about ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, fruit is forbidden as ערלה only for the first three years. The חכמים made this rule stricter for a vine that stays very short. It looks like a new vine, so eating from it could lead people to eat real ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
A young vine less than a handbreadth tall
is forbidden as orla all its years,
because it looks like a one-year-old vine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a list of more rulings from רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vine shorter than a טפח is forbidden as ערלה forever, because it looks like a new vine.

steps.title: The rule applies only to a small group of vines
steps.stepSummary: The ערלה rule applies only to a tiny group of vines. When a whole vineyard is that short, people know the vines are old.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to two vines opposite two vines, with one more sticking out like a tail. But if a whole vineyard is short, people know about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ruling it just gave. The strict rule covers only a small group of vines, not a whole vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole worry was that people would be fooled by how the vine looks. A full vineyard of short old vines is well known. Since people know these vines are old, nobody is fooled and there is no need for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A tail; one vine sticking out from a row
It is well known; people talk about it

phrases.english: And this applies only
to two vines opposite two vines
and one more sticking out like a tail.
But if a whole vineyard is like this,
it is well known.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי שְׁתַּיִם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ערלה ruling of step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule covers only a tiny group of vines. A whole vineyard is well known, so the rule does not apply to it.

steps.title: A dead body takes up four אמות for קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: One may not say קריאת שמע within four אמות of a dead body. This is learned from the פסוק 'Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: A dead person takes up four אמות for קריאת שמע, as it is written: 'Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the next ruling in the list from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. One may not say שמע within four אמות of a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead can no longer do מצוות, so they are like 'the poor' in the פסוק. Doing a מצוה right next to them is like mocking them for what they cannot do.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes up a space of four אמות around it

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
A dead person takes up four cubits
for the recitation of Shema,
as it is written:
"Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker."

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת תּוֹפֵס אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ruling in the list from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not say שמע within four אמות of a dead body.

steps.title: A stepdaughter raised with the brothers may not marry them
steps.stepSummary: A stepdaughter who grows up with her stepfather's sons may not marry them, because she looks like their sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: A stepdaughter who grows up among the brothers may not marry the brothers, because she looks like their sister.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the next ruling in the list from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, now reported by רבי יצחק. A stepdaughter raised in the same house as the sons may not marry them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law she may marry them, because they are not related to her at all. The concern is only about appearance. People might think a man is marrying his real sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Who grows up among the brothers

steps.confusionAlert: She is not actually related to the brothers. The concern is only that she looks like their sister.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
A stepdaughter who grows up among the brothers
is forbidden to marry the brothers,
because she looks like their sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ruling in the list from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stepdaughter raised with the brothers may not marry them, because she looks like their sister.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects the stepdaughter ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the stepdaughter ruling is not correct. People know she is not truly their sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so, because the matter is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא disagrees with the ruling it just quoted. The marriage is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban was that people might be fooled. But family facts like this are well known, so no one will think she is their real sister. The worry falls away, and so does the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so; this ruling is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: These rulings all worry about what people might wrongly think. When a fact is well known (קלא אית ליה), as with a whole vineyard or a stepdaughter's family, the worry is gone and no ban is needed.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
because the matter is well known.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא קָלָא אִית לַיהּ לְמִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the stepdaughter ruling of step 31
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The worry about how it looks does not apply, because people know the real family facts.

steps.title: Gifts for the poor piled at the threshing floor need tithing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that לקט, שכחה and פאה gathered into a pile at the threshing floor become obligated in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: if a person gathered לקט, שכחה or פאה into a pile at the threshing floor, that produce now needs to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from the same chain of names. Produce for the poor that was piled up at the threshing floor must be tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, gifts for the poor are free from מעשר. Once they are piled at the גורן like a regular harvest, onlookers will think it is the owner's own grain. So it is treated as fixed for tithes. This fits the theme of the recent steps: the הלכה follows how things look to others.

keyTerms.meaning: Stalks that fall during harvest and are left for the poor
Sheaves forgotten in the field, which are left for the poor
The corner of the field, left unharvested for the poor
Threshing floor, where grain is piled and processed

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
that one gathered into a pile at the threshing floor
became fixed for tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next ruling in the same list of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rulings about how things appear to onlookers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לקט, שכחה and פאה piled at the threshing floor become obligated in מעשר.

steps.title: עולא limits the ruling to a pile in the field
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the tithing rule applies only when the pile is in the field. In the city, people know the truth about this produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: we only said this when the pile is in the field. In the city, word about the matter gets around, so it does not need tithing.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא narrows the ruling from the step before. It applies only to a pile in the field, not to one in the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ruling was that people might think the produce is the owner's own. In the city 'the matter has a voice': people know this is produce for the poor, so nobody is misled. The same pattern appeared earlier: when people know the facts, the worry of מראית עין falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a limiting formula)
The matter has a voice, meaning it becomes publicly known

phrases.english: Ulla said:
We only said this in the field,
but in the city
the matter has a voice.
phrases.notes: People find out what this produce really is, so nobody is fooled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the tithing ruling of step 33 to a pile in the field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tithing rule applies only in the field. In the city the matter is known, so there is no obligation.
steps.whatToRemember: The worry is only about what onlookers will think. Where people know the truth (in the city), the rule does not apply.

steps.title: A very short young vine does not make nearby seeds forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that a young vine shorter than a טפח does not make the seeds planted near it forbidden as כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: a young vine less than a טפח tall does not make the seeds next to it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling about the same short young vine from steps 28-29. This time the question is כלאים, not ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeds planted near a vineyard normally become forbidden under כלאים הכרם. A vine this small is not treated as a real vine for this purpose, so the seeds stay permitted. It is the same small vine as before, now applied to a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, roughly the width of a hand
Makes forbidden (literally 'sanctifies'), the term for seeds forbidden as כלאים הכרם
Seeds or plantings sown near the vine

steps.confusionAlert: Here מקדשת does not mean 'makes holy' in a good sense. It means the seeds become forbidden because of כלאים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
A young vine that is less than a handbreadth
does not make the seeds forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same chain. It takes the short vine of step 28 and applies it to כלאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young vine under a טפח does not make nearby seeds forbidden as כלאים.

steps.title: The rule applies only to a tiny group of five vines
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is limited to the smallest shape of a vineyard: two vines facing two, with one as a tail. A whole vineyard of short vines does make seeds forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to two vines opposite two, with one sticking out as a tail. But a whole vineyard of such vines does make the seeds forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the ruling from the step before. The leniency covers only a tiny group of five vines, not a full vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facing two, plus one as a tail, is the smallest group of vines that counts as a vineyard. With so few short vines, nobody sees them as a real vineyard. When a whole vineyard is short, people recognize it as a vineyard, so the seeds become forbidden. This matches step 29, where a whole short vineyard was also treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only... (a limiting formula)
Sticking out as a tail, a fifth vine extending past the others

phrases.english: And this applies only to
two vines opposite two
and one sticking out as a tail,
but a whole vineyard
phrases.notes: Some versions spell it כולי, in round brackets. The square brackets give the corrected spelling, כּוּלֵּיהּ.

phrases.english: makes the seeds forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי שְׁתַּיִם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁתַּיִם וְאַחַת יוֹצְאָה זָנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the כלאים leniency of step 35 to a tiny group of vines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a minimal group of five short vines is lenient. A whole short vineyard makes the seeds forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: For both ערלה and כלאים, a whole short vineyard is treated differently from a tiny group of vines. With a full vineyard, people recognize what it really is.

steps.title: Opening the next ruling in the chain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, reported through רבי יצחק and רבי יוחנן. The ruling itself comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. It names who said the next ruling, and the ruling itself follows right after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same opening formula used for each ruling in this list. The ruling it introduces continues on the next דף. Nothing new is ruled yet.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
phrases.notes: The ruling he is about to quote comes right at the start of the next דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the next ruling in the same list of rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attribution only. The ruling it introduces follows in the next part of the text.
